gloss: to bite into, to cut into

definitions.gloss: to bite into, to dig into
definitions.explanation: To physically cut or sink into a surface, like a rope digging into skin or teeth biting into food.

definitions.gloss: to cut into, to eat into
definitions.explanation: To extend into or encroach upon something, especially time, budget, or territory.

definitions.gloss: to make inroads into, to gain a foothold in
definitions.explanation: To penetrate or establish a presence in a market, industry, or area of influence.

examples.japanese: ロープが{肩|かた}に{食|く}い{込|こ}んで{痛|いた}い。
examples.english: The rope is digging into my shoulder and it hurts.

examples.japanese: {残業|ざんぎょう}が{私生活|しせいかつ}に{食|く}い{込|こ}んでいる。
examples.english: Overtime work is eating into my personal life.

examples.japanese: この{会社|かいしゃ}は{海外市場|かいがいしじょう}に{食|く}い{込|こ}むことに{成功|せいこう}した。
examples.english: This company succeeded in making inroads into overseas markets.

notes:
USAGE: {食|く}い{込|こ}む is a compound verb combining {食|く}う (to bite, to eat) and {込|こ}む (into). It expresses penetrating or cutting into something, either physically or figuratively.

TRANSITIVITY: Intransitive ({自動詞|じどうし}). Takes に for what is being penetrated.

ASPECT: {食|く}い{込|こ}んでいる indicates an ongoing state of something cutting or biting into something else.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{肉|にく}に{食|く}い{込|こ}む (to dig into flesh)
・{予算|よさん}に{食|く}い{込|こ}む (to cut into the budget)
・{市場|しじょう}に{食|く}い{込|こ}む (to make inroads into a market)
・{睡眠時間|すいみんじかん}に{食|く}い{込|こ}む (to eat into sleep time)

REGISTER: Neutral. Common in both everyday and business contexts.
